title: AI at Work: Adoption Rises, but Value Lags
description: A fictional workforce research report on enterprise AI adoption, training, workflow redesign, and AI agents.

slides.title:
AI at Work:
Adoption Rises,
but Value Lags
slides.copy: A fictional workforce study on the gap between access and meaningful use.

images.alt: Original luminous green particle sphere on a black background

slides.note: Illustrative research concept — not a real survey

slides.title: Survey parameters
slides.copy: A fictional cross-market sample designed to show a consulting research profile.

slides.title: Four findings from the workforce
slides.copy: Access has spread faster than the practices that turn AI into dependable value.

features.title: Use is common
features.copy: Regular adoption now reaches most office-based roles.

features.title: Frontline use trails
features.copy: Access and time remain uneven across roles.

features.title: Training is thin
features.copy: Many employees learn through trial and error.

features.title: Workflows lag
features.copy: Most teams add tools before changing the work.

slides.title: Adoption is high, but frontline use has stalled
slides.copy: Regular AI use rises with seniority, leaving the employees closest to daily operations behind.
slides.chartLabel: Illustrative share of employees using AI regularly, percent

slides.title: Time savings depend on the work
slides.copy: Employees report the largest gains in repeatable administrative tasks and the smallest gains in professional development.
slides.chartLabel: Illustrative share reporting at least one hour saved on days they use AI, percent

metrics.label: illustrative share saving more than one hour

slides.title: Three barriers shape adoption
slides.copy: Employees need practical instruction, approved tools, and visible support from leaders.

features.title: 38% lack practical training
features.copy: Short sessions explain the tool but rarely change the work.

features.title: 34% lack approved tools
features.copy: Employees turn to unsanctioned options when access is limited.

features.title: 27% lack leadership support
features.copy: Teams hesitate when expectations and accountability stay unclear.

slides.title: Workflow redesign remains uneven
slides.copy: Most companies deploy AI inside existing processes. Fewer reshape the work or invent a different model.
slides.note: Illustrative survey data; categories may overlap

slides.title: AI agents show promise, but understanding remains low
slides.copy: Interest is broad. Familiarity with governance, limits, and day-to-day use remains narrow.

features.title: 31% understand agents
features.copy: Practical familiarity remains much lower than interest.

features.title: 42% worry about oversight
features.copy: Another 35% cite unclear accountability when mistakes occur.

slides.title: Four priorities for leaders
slides.copy: The next phase depends on practical capability and deliberate workflow choices.

features.title: Train for the work
features.copy: Teach employees inside real tasks and decisions.

features.title: Measure value
features.copy: Track time, quality, satisfaction, and risk.

features.title: Redesign workflows
features.copy: Change the process when tools alone stop helping.
